extracted.intended_audience: Members of the public, stakeholders, regulated entities, and attorneys who may submit comments on the EPA proposed consent decree (NESHAP Polyether Polyols)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and legal notice for submitting public comments on a proposed EPA consent decree under the Clean Air Act (NESHAP for Polyether Polyols). Includes docket access, submission procedures, and statutory context for the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment deadline / timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments on the proposed consent decree must be received by October 10, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure comments are submitted within the specified comment period. Comments received after the close of the comment period will be marked 'late.' The EPA is not required to consider late comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify submissions with correct Docket ID
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions received must include the Docket ID number for this action (Docket ID No. EPA-HQ-OGC-2024-0394).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit your comments identified by Docket ID No. EPA-HQ-OGC-2024-0394. Failure to include the Docket ID may impede the agency's ability to associate your comment with this action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission method: regulations.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your comments, identified by Docket ID No., online at https://www.regulations.gov (EPA's preferred method).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online instructions for submitting comments. Use https://www.regulations.gov to submit or view public comments, access the index of the official public docket, and access electronically-available docket documents. The electronic public docket system is 'anonymous access'—EPA will not know your identity unless you include it in the body of your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments cannot be edited or removed after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed from this docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review your comment carefully before submission because you cannot change or withdraw it later.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA may publish, redact, or withhold submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments received may be posted without change to https://www.regulations.gov, including any personal information provided. Be aware that EPA may redact or withhold content where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit Confidential Business Information (CBI) via public docket
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit to EPA's docket at https://www.regulations.gov any information you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For additional submission methods, the full EPA public comment policy, and information about CBI or multimedia submissions, visit https://www.epa.gov/dockets/commenting-epa-dockets. For CBI submitted by mail, expect possible delays and that deliveries or couriers will be received by scheduled appointment only. Contact the person listed in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT for CBI submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia submissions must be accompanied by a written comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment. The written comment is considered the official comment and should include discussion of all points you wish to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submit multimedia, include a written narrative covering everything you want the agency to consider; the agency treats the written text as the official submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content located outside primary submission generally not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on external links or hosted files as the substance of your comment. If you must include outside materials, ensure essential content is contained in the primary written submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contact information in comment body (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit an electronic comment, EPA recommends that you include your name, mailing address, and an email address or other contact information in the body of your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including contact info ensures EPA can identify and contact you if the agency cannot read your comment or needs further information. Any identifying/contact information in the comment body will be included in the official public docket and made available publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public docket access and where to obtain proposed consent decree
rubrics_metrics.description: The official public docket for this action (Docket ID No. EPA-HQ-OGC-2024-0394) contains a copy of the proposed consent decree and is available for public viewing at the OEI Docket in the EPA Docket Center and electronically through https://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading room hours: 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding legal holidays. Telephone numbers provided for the Public Reading Room and OEI Docket are available in the notice. Use the docket ID to search and access documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and public posting implications
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic public docket system is an 'anonymous access' system, which means EPA will not know your identity, email address, or other contact information unless you provide it in the body of your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, any identifying information you include in the comment body will appear in the public docket. Comments may be posted without change, so avoid including sensitive personal information in the comment text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency may withdraw or withhold consent based on comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA or the Department of Justice may withdraw or withhold consent to the proposed consent decree if the comments disclose facts or considerations that indicate that such consent is inappropriate, improper, inadequate, or inconsistent with the requirements of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive comments that reveal legal or factual problems with the consent decree can affect whether the agency gives final approval to the consent decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory legal bases described (criteria for agency obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice cites Clean Air Act section 112(d)(6) (requirement to review NESHAP at least every eight years) and alleges agency delay under Clean Air Act section 304(a); it references 40 CFR part 63, subpart PPP (Polyether Polyols Production NESHAP) and the 2014 NESHAP (79 FR 17340).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory/regulatory citations explain the legal obligations at issue and the basis for the plaintiffs' claims and for the terms of the proposed consent decree. Comments that address whether the consent decree appropriately implements these statutory duties are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific consent decree deadlines and required actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed consent decree would require by December 10, 2024 that EPA sign (1) a final rule taking action on reconsideration of the affirmative defense provisions related to the 2014 NESHAP for Polyether Polyols (40 CFR part 63, subpart PPP), and (2) a notice of proposed rulemaking on its review of the NESHAP for the Polyether Polyols Production source category, including all 'necessary' revisions. By December 10, 2025, EPA would sign a final rule for these proposed actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may address the appropriateness, feasibility, or legality of these deadlines and the specific actions required by the consent decree.
